'''Nancy S. Lacore''' (born 1968/1969)<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bailey |first1=Steve |title=Bailey: Move over Nancy Mace, there's a new Nancy in town, and she's an admiral |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/opinion/commentary/nancy-lacore-first-congressional-district-democratic-nomination/article_70cc6698-f391-4536-80c5-36d896bdad7e.html |access-date=October 24, 2026 |work=[[The Post and Courier]] |date=January 22, 2026 |location=[[Charleston, South Carolina]] |language=en}}</ref> is a retired [[United States Navy]] officer and political candidate who served as the 16th [[Chief of Navy Reserve]] from 2024 to 2025.<ref name="Slayton-2025" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Toropin |first=Konstantin |last2=Jalonick |first2=Mary Clare |last3=Price |first3=Michelle L. |date=22 August 2025 |title=Hegseth fires general whose agency's intel assessment of damage from Iran strikes angered Trump |url=https://apnews.com/article/pentagon-dia-iran-intelligence-trump-kruse-5cb1fb89b8f12c3b517f139f6d840b48 |access-date=11 May 2026 |work=[[AP News]] |language=en-US}}</ref> A [[Vice admiral (United States)|vice admiral]], she previously served as the 93rd commandant of [[Naval District Washington]] from 2022 to 2024. She also served as the director of the Maritime Partnership Program, U.S. Naval Forces Europe/Africa/U.S. 6th Fleet, with additional duties as vice commander of [[U.S. 6th Fleet]] in Naples, Italy.<ref name="SIGNAL-2018">{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.afcea.org/signal-media/lacore-assigned-director-maritime-partnership-program |title=Lacore Assigned Director of Maritime Partnership Program |date=6 December 2018 |magazine=[[SIGNAL Magazine]] |language=en |access-date=3 March 2019}}</ref>

Lacore was the Democratic nominee for the [[2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_South_Carolina#District_1|South Carolina 1st congressional district in 2026]], seeking to fill the seat being vacated by Republican incumbent [[Nancy Mace]], whose term will expire in 2027. She won the election in a flip for Democrats and will be sworn into office in January 2027.

== Career ==
Lacore graduated in 1990 from the [[College of the Holy Cross]] with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree and received her commission from the [[Naval Reserve Officer Training Corps]] program. She earned a [[Master of Arts]] from [[San Diego State University]] and is a graduate of the [[Air Command and Staff College]], and the [[National Defense University (Washington, D.C.)|National Defense University]] at the [[Joint Forces Staff College]]. She was designated a [[United States Naval Aviator|Naval Aviator]] in 1993.

Her flying tours include Helicopter Combat Support Squadrons 8 in Norfolk, Virginia and 3 in San Diego, California, as well as Commander, Helicopter Tactical Wing Pacific. She affiliated with the [[United States Navy Reserve|Navy Reserve]] in 2000.

Lacore's staff assignments include Navy Reserve (NR) Naval Air Wings Pacific in San Diego, California, and NR Commander Amphibious Squadron 4 Detachment 104 in Bessemer, Alabama. She served as the executive officer of NR Tactical Air Control Squadron 2186 and NR Commander Strike Force Training Atlantic, and as the chief staff officer for NR Commander 2nd Fleet Joint Force Air Component Commander, in Norfolk, Virginia. She mobilized to serve as the chief of Key Leader Engagement at Headquarters, International Security Assistance Force in [[Kabul]], [[Afghanistan]], from 2011 to 2012.

Her command tours include NR Commander Destroyer Squadron 40 Headquarters in Jacksonville, Florida; NR Commander, U.S. Naval Forces Europe-Africa/U.S. 6th Fleet Maritime Partnership Program Detachment 413 in Detroit, Michigan; and NR U.S. Fleet Forces Command Maritime and Air Operations Headquarters in Norfolk, Virginia. She served in a post-command assignment as the Navy Reserve chief staff officer at U.S. Fleet Forces in 2017, from which she mobilized to serve as the commanding officer, [[Camp Lemonnier]], [[Djibouti]].

Lacore was promoted to rear admiral (lower half) in 2018.<ref name="SIGNAL-2018" /> She was promoted to rear admiral on 1 October 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mynavyhr.navy.mil/Portals/55/Career/Detailing/Flag/October%202021%20Roster%20Public.pdf?ver=0v-yZeh3-fCOfAr1rllvKA%3d% |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211002040112/https://www.mynavyhr.navy.mil/Portals/55/Career/Detailing/Flag/October%202021%20Roster%20Public.pdf?ver=0v-yZeh3-fCOfAr1rllvKA%3D% |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 October 2021 |title=United States Navy Flag Officers (Public) |access-date=2 October 2021}}</ref> In March 2022, Lacore was reassigned as commandant of [[Naval District Washington]], succeeding [[Michael Steffen]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.war.gov/News/Releases/Release/Article/2964521/flag-officer-assignments/ |title=Flag Officer Assignments |date=11 March 2022 |access-date=12 March 2022 |language=en-US |website=U.S. Department of Defense}}</ref> She assumed command on 10 June 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mynavyhr.navy.mil/Portals/55/Career/Detailing/Flag/May%202022%20Roster%20Public.pdf?ver=bwlOxO7rLP6GQGaNsPhu4g%3d%3d |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220430065122/https://www.mynavyhr.navy.mil/Portals/55/Career/Detailing/Flag/May%202022%20Roster%20Public.pdf?ver=bwlOxO7rLP6GQGaNsPhu4g%3D%3D |url-status=dead |archive-date=30 April 2022|title=United States Navy Flag Officers (Public), May 2022|date=30 April 2022|website=MyNavyHR}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Kersting |first=Griffin |url=https://www.dvidshub.net/news/422713/commandant-naval-district-washington-changes-command |title=Commandant, Naval District Washington, Changes Command |date=10 June 2022 |access-date=11 June 2022 |publisher=Naval District Washington |location=[[Washington Navy Yard]], [[Washington, D. C.]] |website=DVIDS}}</ref>

In May 2024, Lacore was nominated for promotion to vice admiral and assignment as [[chief of Navy Reserve]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.congress.gov/nomination/118th-congress/1762?s=1&r=1 |title=PN1762 — Rear Adm. Nancy S. Lacore — Navy |website=U.S. Congress |date=14 May 2024}}</ref> She was relieved of her duties on 22 August 2025, by Secretary of War (Defense) Pete Hegseth.<ref name="Slayton-2025">{{Cite web |last=Slayton |first=Nicholas |date=23 August 2025 |title=Pentagon fires heads of Navy Reserve, Naval Special Warfare Command |url=https://taskandpurpose.com/news/navy-fires-reserve-special-warfare-command/ |website=[[Task & Purpose]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Strobel |first=Warren P. |last2=Robertson |first2=Noah |last3=Lamothe |first3=Dan |date=22 August 2025 |title=Hegseth fires head of Defense Intelligence Agency, Lt. Gen. Jeffrey Kruse |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2025/08/22/defense-intelligence-agency-kruse-fired-hegseth/ |access-date=23 August 2025 |work=The Washington Post |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286 |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250822184334/https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2025/08/22/defense-intelligence-agency-kruse-fired-hegseth/ |archive-date=22 August 2025 |quote=Others removed include Vice Adm. Nancy Lacore, the chief of the Navy Reserve}}</ref>

== Activities ==
After returning from Afghanistan in 2012, she started volunteering for Wounded Wear, a Chesapeake-based nonprofit that helps families of service members who were killed or seriously injured. She later joined the organization's board.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://pilotonline.com/news/military/article_2296304e-ee13-51c1-b1cc-a7ca2b84ae85.html |title=Woman to run 160 miles for fallen service members |last=Reilly |first=Corinne |newspaper=[[The Virginian-Pilot]] |language=en |access-date=3 March 2019 |date=19 August 2014 |archive-date=6 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306043608/https://pilotonline.com/news/military/article_2296304e-ee13-51c1-b1cc-a7ca2b84ae85.html |url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2014, she established "Valor Knows No Gender: Run to Remember", a 160-mile run, in 160 hours, for the 160 female veterans who died while serving in Iraq and Afghanistan.<ref>{{Cite news |first1=Tom |last1=Giusto |first2=Ali |last2=Weinberg |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/extra-mile-navy-captain-runs-honor-fallen-servicewomen/story?id=26820411 |title=Going the Extra Mile: Navy Captain Runs to Honor Fallen Servicewomen |date=11 November 2014 |work=ABC News |language=en |access-date=3 March 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.andisuephillips.com/latest-post/ |title=160 Miles in 160 Hours to Honor 160 Lives {{!}} Andi Sue |first=Andi Sue |last=Phillips |date=2 September 2016 |website=andisuephillips.com |language=en-US |access-date=3 March 2019}}</ref> In 2018, she joined the Women's Panel Event in Djibouti, dedicated to Women's History Month and International Women's Day.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.africom.mil/media-room/Article/30511/u-s-ambassador-to-djibouti-sponsors-womens-panel-event |title=U.S. Ambassador to Djibouti sponsors Women's Panel Event |author=Lt. Desiree Woodman |date=27 March 2018 |website=United States Africa Command |access-date=3 March 2019}}</ref>

== 2026 U.S. House of Representatives campaign ==
{{main|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in South Carolina#District 1}}
In January 2026, Lacore announced her candidacy for the Democratic nomination in [[South Carolina's 1st congressional district]] for the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in South Carolina]], a seat occupied by Republican [[Nancy Mace]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Thompson |first1=Marissa |date=20 January 2026 |title=Navy veteran announces run to represent SC's First Congressional District |url=https://www.live5news.com/2026/01/20/navy-veteran-announces-run-represent-scs-first-congressional-district/ |access-date=20 January 2026 |work=[[WCSC-TV]] |language=en}}</ref> Endorsed by the [[Blue Dog Coalition|Blue Dog PAC]]<ref>https://bluedogdems.com/nancy-lacore/</ref>, Lacore achieved the highest number of votes, 36.5%, in the 9 June primary election, advancing to a run-off against Mac Deford.<ref>{{Cite news |date=10 June 2026 |title=South Carolina U.S. House primary results |url=https://apnews.com/projects/elections-2026/south-carolina-primary-results-us-house/#1 |access-date=10 June 2026 |work=[[AP News]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=10 June 2026 |title=GUIDE: What to know about runoff elections in South Carolina |url=https://www.wistv.com/2026/06/10/what-know-about-runoff-elections-south-carolina/ |access-date=10 June 2026 |work=[[WIS (TV)]] News}}</ref>

After defeating Deford 52.1%-47.9% in the 23 June runoff, Lacore became the Democratic nominee for the South Carolina 1st congressional district seat.<ref>{{cite news |last=Corasaniti |first=Nick |title=Fired Navy Admiral Wins Democratic Runoff in South Carolina's 1st District |date=24 June 2026 |issn=0362-4331 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/23/us/politics/nancy-lacore-nancy-mace-south-carolina-house-democrats.html |language=en-US |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref>

Lacore went on to flip the district from Republican to Democrat, defeating Republican Jenny Costa Honeycutt.<ref name="ThompsonKirschner2026-1">{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=Marissa |last2=Kirschner |first2=Gracie |date=2026-11-04 |title=Lacore claims SC-01 victory, says Costa Honeycutt conceded race |url=https://www.live5news.com/2026/11/04/lacore-claims-sc-01-victory-says-costa-honeycutt-conceded-race/ |access-date=2026-11-05 |website=https://www.live5news.com |language=en}}</ref>  

== Awards ==
Lacore's personal awards include the [[Legion of Merit]], [[Defense Meritorious Service Medal]], [[Meritorious Service Medal (United States)|Meritorious Service Medal]], [[Navy Commendation Medal]], [[Navy Achievement Medal]], and other campaign and unit commendations. She accumulated approximately 1300 flight hours in military aircraft.

== Personal life ==
Lacore is married to Patrick Lacore.<ref>{{Cite news |date=11 November 2014 |title=Virginia veteran runs 160 miles in 160 hours to honor fallen servicewomen |url=https://wjla.com/features/veterans/virginia-veteran-runs-160-miles-in-160-hours-to-honor-fallen-servicewomen-108929 |access-date=10 June 2026 |work=[[WJLA-TV]] |language=en}}</ref> They have six children – five daughters and a son.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.poshseven.com/nancy-lacore.html |title=Nancy Lacore |date=26 April 2010 |website=Posh Seven Magazine for Women in Loudoun |language=en-US |access-date=3 March 2019 |archive-date=6 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306044443/https://www.poshseven.com/nancy-lacore.html |url-status=dead}}</ref>
